name: Baoding · rural AI-assisted cervical cytology
short: Retrospective rural screening report; historical comparisons and incomplete follow-up limit causal interpretation.
outcome: The AI period reported 863 abnormal cytology results, 542 colposcopies, 20 high-grade lesions and one cervical cancer. These are service counts, not sensitivity estimates. Increased positivity relative to earlier years does not prove better cancer outcomes; follow-up was incomplete.
partners: Baoding Maternal and Child Health Hospital; Handan First Hospital; Hebei University. Baoding basic research grant 2372P003.
followUp: Seek complete biopsy/treatment follow-up and a contemporaneous comparison; verify how women lost to follow-up were handled.
contact: Use the publication correspondence details; no telephone independently verified.
editNotes: Multilingual literature review; limitations and follow-up recorded; not evidence of AI-attributable mortality reduction.

name: Xuzhou · rural AI cytology and HPV triage
metricLabel: Abnormal cytology positivity: AI-assisted versus manual
short: Rural free-screening comparison; positivity rates should not be confused with diagnostic sensitivity.
outcome: The retrospective comparison included 25,007 manually read smears and 54,353 AI-assisted smears, including AI plus HPV triage. Abnormal cytology positivity was 2.78% versus 5.07%. Nonrandomized groups and selective biopsy limit interpretation; these results do not establish reduced cancer incidence or mortality.
partners: Xuzhou screening investigators: He Xuemei, Huang Hui, Wang Ting, Du Hui, Jiang Mengyu and Liang Hui; Journal of Xuzhou Medical University. Funding not verified.
followUp: Check referral completion, histological endpoints and comparability across screening periods. The journal issue is 2022; do not substitute an aggregator posting date.

name: Duke Pocket Colposcopy · multicontrast referral algorithm
short: Multinational referral-image research; the map currently marks the US research lead, not the full study footprint.
outcome: Paired acetic-acid and green-light images from 880 visits supported model development; reported test sensitivity was 75% and specificity 88%. The dataset pooled six countries. Participants were already screening-positive; some negative reference labels were based on visual assessment without biopsy. Performance therefore cannot be generalized to primary population screening.
partners: Duke University and collaborating clinical teams; PATH and international partners. The article acknowledges NSF, ONR, Simons Foundation and NGA support.
geo: US research lead; six-country pooled referral dataset (complete country allocation pending verification)
followUp: Confirm the complete six-country dataset allocation before adding all study-country markers. Seek external prospective validation and treatment-completion outcomes.

name: Kigali · deep-learning cervical histopathology
short: Laboratory biopsy-image study; not a community screening deployment.
outcome: EfficientNetB0 reported 99% test accuracy, 98% sensitivity, 100% specificity and AUC 0.99. These are internal image-classification results from a single setting. They do not establish patient-level screening accuracy, prospective clinical benefit or improved treatment completion.
partners: University of Rwanda; University Teaching Hospital of Kigali; CIIC-HIN and collaborators. Funding not independently verified.
status: Published laboratory study · external validation needed
followUp: Verify patient-level separation of training/test images, sampling and reference labeling. Seek external multicentre and prospective validation before describing this as a screening service.

name: Khayelitsha · AI cervical-imaging implementation preparation
short: Study of implementation conditions in a disadvantaged community; AI effectiveness was not established.
outcome: Two providers screened 75 women while evaluating imaging equipment and implementation conditions. The study identifies workflow, image quality, infrastructure and training considerations. partners: University of Cape Town; Columbia University; Khayelitsha Site B Primary Health Care Clinic. NIH/NCI grants R01CA254576 and R01CA250011.

sampleDetails: 886 selected Korean images; separate 44-participant Indonesian study.
name: Cerviray AI · Korean reader trial and Indonesian field report
status: Randomized reader study + small field comparison
geo: Two Korean centres; West Java, Indonesia · distinct study cohorts
metricLabel: Korean reader sensitivity with versus without AI
short: Strong Korean reader results did not translate directly into a small Indonesian VIA-comparison study.
outcome:
Korea 2023: four readers assessed 886 images in a crossover study. Assisted sensitivity was 89.18% versus 71.33%; specificity 96.68% versus 92.16%. Indonesia 2025: 44 participants, with VIA as reference, gave AI sensitivity 42.9% and specificity 100%; expert image assessment was more sensitive (71.4%). Assessment: useful reader support but limited field transportability. The Indonesian result measures agreement with imperfect VIA, not biopsy-confirmed disease. Neither study establishes population mortality benefit.

Additional West Bandung community study (2026; 71 women): sensitivity 66.7% and specificity 95.6% against VIA, with a very wide sensitivity interval. This uses Cerviray AI and is attached here rather than duplicated. VIA agreement is not histology-confirmed CIN2+ accuracy.
partners: CHA University and Korea University; AIDOT technology; Indonesian clinical collaborators. Korean trial support: CHA University grant 2021-08-001; Indonesian sponsor not verified.
contact: Published research correspondence; direct project telephone not verified. Contact details have not been tested.
followUp: Reconcile cohort overlap with the earlier Indonesian field report; seek larger histology-referenced validation. Supporting report: https://doi.org/10.2147/IJWH.S585614

sampleDetails: Field implementation; AI did not direct routine care.
name: PRESCRIP-TEC / SAKHI AI decision support
short: Women accepted the device with privacy safeguards; images supported remote review. Field performance lagged laboratory testing, and AI remained research-only.
outcome:
September 2026 report: the mobile AI device was feasible but difficult to operate during clinic screening. Images supported remote second opinions and training. Field performance was poorer than laboratory performance; further tuning was needed. AI did not direct routine care. No treatment benefit is established by this implementation study.

The 2026 Bangladesh/Uganda implementation report describes 1,183 uses and practical limitations: field performance below laboratory performance, image quality, staffing and training. It does not establish AI-attributable cancer prevention.
partners: EU Horizon 2020, grant 964270. UMC Groningen, Uganda Cancer Institute, Manipal Academy, Friendship Bangladesh, icddr,b, URDT and Leiden UMC. The wider project ended in January 2024.
contact: Research contact published with Jaap Koot’s UMC Groningen affiliation. Not telephone-verified; not a patient booking line.
followUp: Monitor algorithm refinement, poor-image rejection, clinical specificity and routine-service readiness. Supporting report: https://formative.jmir.org/2026/1/e81493

name: African AVE Collaborative
short: AI-assisted visual inspection detected 71.8% of significant precancers, versus 36.6% with visual inspection alone.
outcome:
Published 2026. Of 24,447 participants, 39% were living with HIV. AI plus visual inspection achieved 71.8% sensitivity, with more false positives than visual inspection alone. HPV testing achieved 90.4% sensitivity. Outcomes are pooled across countries.

Earlier Zambia internal validation (2024; 8,204 women) reported AUC 0.91, sensitivity 85% and specificity 86% at a selected threshold. These development estimates are not directly comparable with later five-country field estimates.
partners: Funded by Unitaid and Global Health Labs. Implemented by CHAI, ministries of health and clinical/research partners.
contact: CHAI headquarters. Ask for the cervical-cancer / AVE team; not a direct investigator line.
followUp: Keep development and external field results distinct; review false negatives, referral burden and treatment completion.
